title: Robotic register
description: A flat, mechanical, affectless register (clipped declaratives, procedural phrasing, timestamps and status lines, no evaluative words, no warmth, no hedging), against the shared neutral scaffold: the same sixteen ordinary situations told plainly. It is a register control for the emotion set: it is expected to sit off the valence/arousal plane (near its origin, and opposite tender if anywhere). Lines are padded with procedural detail so it is not a length direction. The task gives everyday exchanges where both replies carry the same information; the target is the mechanical reply, against a friendly, apologetic, enthusiastic or neutral-polite one.
inspiration: Russell's circumplex of affect (valence x arousal): a control expected near the origin, off the plane

learned.request: One of nine emotion-set corpora: the same sixteen ordinary situations rewritten in one tone, against a shared neutral scaffold, with a task pitting that tone against a neutral reply or a near neighbour; robotic as a register control expected off the valence and arousal plane.
